message.content: {"candidates":[{"stem":"In `charge_with_retry`, the retry after a timeout sends a key to `Client::charge`. Given how `charge` documents the provider's handling of keys, what does the provider do with this retry request if the first request had already reached it and been processed?","options":[{"letter":"A","text":"It returns the receipt from the first charge","rationale":"Correct. The doc comment on `charge` says a request with a key the provider has already seen returns the first charge's receipt. The retry now reuses the original key, so a first attempt that succeeded before timing out is not charged again."},{"letter":"B","text":"It creates a second charge for the same amount","rationale":"Wrong. This is what happened before the change, when the retry used a freshly generated `OperationKey`, which the provider had not seen. With the original key, the provider recognises the request."},{"letter":"C","text":"It rejects the request with an error to the caller","rationale":"Wrong. The doc comment says a repeated key returns the first charge's receipt, not an error. Nothing in `charge` or `charge_with_retry` shows a rejection path for repeated keys."}],"answer_key":"A","why_it_matters":"A timeout does not say whether the provider processed the charge, so the money rule depends on how the provider treats repeated keys.","rubric":[{"statement":"A repeated key makes the provider treat the retry as the same charge, so a first attempt that went through is returned rather than charged again.","met":"Reasoning says the provider recognises the reused key and hands back the first charge's result instead of charging a second time. Any wording that establishes this counts, including by implication.","not_met":"Reasoning claims the retry creates a new charge or an error, or does not connect the reused key to the provider's recognising the earlier charge."}],"hint":"Read the doc comment above `charge` in src/payments/client.rs alongside the lines that build the key in the timeout branch.","citations":[{"path":"src/payments/client.rs","first_line":12,"last_line":16},{"path":"src/payments/retry.rs","first_line":3,"last_line":6}]},{"stem":"A timeout from the first `client.charge` call in `charge_with_retry` leaves it unknown whether the provider processed that request. Which key must the retry carry for the customer to be charged for `original.amount` no more than once?","options":[{"letter":"A","text":"A new key generated for the retry attempt","rationale":"Wrong. This was the old behaviour. The provider charges at most once per key, so a new key looks like a different charge and could duplicate a first attempt that had succeeded."},{"letter":"B","text":"The same key the first attempt carried","rationale":"Correct. The provider deduplicates by key, so the retry must carry `original.key` for it to be recognised as the same charge as the first attempt."},{"letter":"C","text":"A key derived from the charge amount","rationale":"Wrong. The provider only matches keys it has seen. A key derived from the amount is not the key of the first request, and different charges of the same amount would also collide."}],"answer_key":"B","why_it_matters":"The rule that one logical charge maps to one key is what stops customers being billed twice when the outcome of a request is unknown.","rubric":[{"statement":"Because the outcome of the first attempt is unknown after a timeout, the retry must be identifiable to the provider as the same charge, which requires the same key as the first attempt.","met":"Reasoning ties the unknown outcome of the timed-out request to the need for the provider to match the retry with the first request through an identical key. Any wording that establishes this counts.","not_met":"Reasoning treats a fresh or derived key as adequate, or does not explain why the retry must be recognisable as the same charge."}],"hint":"Compare the key passed in the first call on line 2 with the one built in the timeout branch, and check what `charge` says about keys.","citations":[{"path":"src/payments/retry.rs","first_line":1,"last_line":9},{"path":"src/payments/client.rs","first_line":12,"last_line":15}]}]}
